headline: Contracts verified on Etherscan with two recognized audits, but no public GitHub repo and USDf/sUSDf audits are >12 months stale
short_headline: Verified; stale audits, no public repo

findings.text: USDf proxy (0xFa2B947eEc368f42195f24F36d2aF29f7c24CeC2) is verified on Etherscan as an EIP-1967 Transparent Proxy, with implementation at 0x3aDf34C09DAC24E4BAeFB1b1df4C2992edC2b789 also verified (ABI source: etherscan per DeFiPunkd surfacer). sUSDf proxy (0xc8CF6D7991f15525488b2A83Df53468D682Ba4B0) is likewise verified as a TransparentUpgradeableProxy with a separately verified implementation at 0x0D132bEE...1BfDa3F34 per Etherscan search results showing source code fragments.

No public GitHub repository is recorded for Falcon Finance (protocol.github is empty). Search found no canonical source-code repo. Source-to-deployed-bytecode correspondence cannot be confirmed; no commit SHA can be pinned.

Three audits are listed on the docs page: (1) Zellic covered USDf & sUSDf, assessment February 11–17 2025, report released March 7 2025; (2) Pashov covered USDf & sUSDf, report dated 2025-02-17; (3) Zellic covered FF token, assessment September 18 2025. The USDf/sUSDf audits are approximately 15 months prior to the analysis date (May 2026), exceeding the 6-month threshold. No follow-up review for USDf/sUSDf post-deployment was found. Direct PDF fetch of all three reports was blocked.
Zellic is a broadly recognized Solidity security firm. Pashov Audit Group is a recognized boutique Solidity auditor. Both qualify under the recognized-firm list.

Post-audit drift cannot be assessed: no public GitHub repo exists to compare audited commit against currently deployed source. The absence of a repo is recorded as an unknowns entry. The FF token received a September 2025 Zellic audit (~8 months prior to analysis date), which is within the threshold.

Both USDf and sUSDf are proxies. Etherscan search results confirm source code is present for both the proxy contracts AND their implementation contracts separately (implementation addresses surfaced via Etherscan's proxy-resolution). A verified proxy with a verified implementation is satisfied for both core token contracts.

steelman.red: No public GitHub repo means the audited commit cannot be independently matched to deployed bytecode, and the primary USDf/sUSDf audits are 15 months stale with no confirmed follow-up—an outsider cannot fully verify what the deployed code does relative to any audited reference.
steelman.orange: Both proxy and implementation contracts are Etherscan-verified with source code visible; two recognised firms (Zellic, Pashov) audited the core USDf/sUSDf contracts; the FF token received a more recent Zellic audit (Sept 2025). The staleness of the USDf/sUSDf audits and absence of a public repo prevent a green grade.
steelman.green: All core contracts are source-verified on Etherscan, two reputable firms audited USDf/sUSDf, both proxies and their implementations are verified, and the protocol is actively maintained with audits from recognised firms—verifiability posture is strong for a relatively young protocol.

rationale.verdict: Choosing orange because the USDf and sUSDf contracts are Etherscan-verified (proxy + implementation) and were audited by two recognised firms (Zellic and Pashov), but (1) the core USDf/sUSDf audits date from February 2025—approximately 15 months before the analysis date—with no confirmed follow-up review covering those contracts, exceeding the 6-month staleness threshold; and (2) no public GitHub repository exists, making independent source-to-bytecode correspondence impossible to confirm. The green steelman is weaker because audit staleness and missing repo are concrete verifiability gaps for fund-custody contracts.

evidence.shows: USDf proxy contract on Ethereum; ABI source confirmed as 'etherscan' (verified); proxy resolves to implementation 0x3aDf34C09DAC24E4BAeFB1b1df4C2992edC2b789 via EIP-1967 pattern; contract name 'Falcon USD' / symbol 'USDf'
Three audits listed: (1) Zellic – USDf & sUSDf, (2) Pashov – USDf & sUSDf (report 2025-02-17), (3) Zellic – FF token. All reported no critical/high vulnerabilities.
Zellic conducted a security assessment for Falcon from February 11th to February 17th, 2025 (USDf & sUSDf scope). Confirms Zellic as auditor and assessment window.
Zellic conducted a security assessment for Falcon Finance (FF token) on September 18th, 2025. Confirms a more recent Zellic audit for the FF governance token.

Etherscan confirms ABI is sourced from the implementation contract at 0x3adf34c09dac24e4baefb1b1df4c2992edc2b789 using the EIP-1967 Transparent Proxy pattern, indicating both proxy and implementation are verified on Etherscan.

sUSDf proxy is verified on Etherscan as a TransparentUpgradeableProxy (OZ v5.1.0) with a separately identified implementation at 0x0D132bEE...1BfDa3F34, confirming source-verified proxy + implementation for sUSDf.
Confirms first audit reports from Zellic and Pashov Audit Group were released in Q1 2025, corroborating the Feb 2025 audit dates.

protocol_metadata.about: Falcon Finance is a basis-trading synthetic dollar protocol that lets users mint USDf, an overcollateralized synthetic dollar, by depositing stablecoins or volatile assets as collateral. Users can stake USDf to receive sUSDf, a yield-bearing ERC-4626 token that accrues returns from institutional-grade delta-neutral strategies including funding-rate arbitrage and cross-exchange arbitrage. Fixed-term restaking of sUSDf issues an ERC-721 position NFT representing the locked stake and boosted yield entitlement. The FF governance token governs the protocol via an independent foundation.
